references.text: The fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy: Peter denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed, just as Jesus predicted in this verse. See [ref:Luk 22:54-62|Luke 22:54-62].
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus tells Peter that he will deny him three times before the rooster crows. See [ref:Matt 26:34-35|Matthew 26:34-35].
Mark's parallel account where Jesus specifically says that Peter will deny him three times before the rooster crows twice. See [ref:Mark 14:30-31|Mark 14:30-31].
John's parallel account where Jesus predicts Peter's denial: "Truly, truly, I say to you: The rooster will not crow before you have denied me three times." See [ref:Joh 13:38|John 13:38].
Matthew's account of the actual fulfillment of Jesus' words, where Peter denies knowing Jesus three times, and then the rooster crows. See [ref:Matt 26:69-75|Matthew 26:69-75].
Mark's account of Peter's three denials and the rooster's crowing, fulfilling Jesus' prophecy. See [ref:Mark 14:66-72|Mark 14:66-72].
John's account of Peter's first and second denial in the high priest's courtyard. See [ref:Joh 18:15-18|John 18:15-18].
John's account of Peter's third denial, followed by the rooster crowing – the final fulfillment of Jesus' words. See [ref:Joh 18:25-27|John 18:25-27].
After the resurrection, Jesus asks Peter three times "Do you love me?" – once for each denial – and restores him to service. See [ref:Joh 21:15-17|John 21:15-17].

The immediate context where Jesus warns Peter that Satan has demanded to sift the disciples like wheat, and Peter assures that he is willing to go to prison and to death with Jesus. See [ref:Luk 22:31-33|Luke 22:31-33].
